markets.name: Hackescher Markt
markets.line: Brandenburg fruit and veg, cheese, fish rolls and lahmacun on the square right by the S-Bahn arches.
markets.walk: On the doorstep of the old centre, so it needs no separate trip.

markets.name: Winterfeldtplatz
markets.line: The biggest and best known weekly market in the city, and the one that feels like a Saturday event rather than an errand.
markets.walk: Saturday is the long day here; Wednesday packs up at 14:00.

markets.name: Maybachufer (Turkish market)
markets.line: A canal-side row of fabric, herbs, olives, cheese and gözleme that only starts at 11:00 and runs into the evening.
markets.walk: The one market you can still reach after a long museum morning.

markets.name: Ökomarkt Kollwitzplatz
markets.line: Around forty certified organic traders under the trees, run by the environmental group Grüne Liga since the late 1990s.
markets.walk: Closes an hour earlier, at 18:00, from January to March.

markets.name: Kollwitzplatz Saturday market
markets.line: The Saturday version is broader and much more about eating: currywurst, crepes, falafel, fish rolls, oysters.

markets.name: Boxhagener Platz
markets.line: Running since 1905 and the oldest weekly market in the eastern half of the city, wrapped around a green square.
markets.walk: Do not confuse it with the Sunday flea market on the same square.

markets.name: Karl-August-Platz
markets.line: Trading since 1894, with over a hundred stalls of produce, cheese, fresh pasta and cut flowers beside the church.
markets.walk: The west-side option if you are staying near Ku'damm.

markets.name: Arkonaplatz
markets.line: Twenty-five to thirty-five traders, a lot of it organic, plus waffles and grilled fish next to a large playground.
markets.walk: A Friday afternoon market, not a morning one.

markets.name: Ökomarkt Chamissoplatz
markets.line: A small organic market on one of the few Kreuzberg squares that kept its nineteenth-century facades intact.
markets.walk: Worth it as much for the square as for the stalls.

markets.name: Ökomarkt Hohenstaufenplatz
markets.line: Organic produce about ten minutes on foot from the Maybachufer, which makes a Tuesday double possible without a train.
markets.walk: Pairs with the Turkish market on a Tuesday.

markets.name: Südstern
markets.line: A calm neighbourhood Saturday market at the end of Bergmannstraße, good if the bigger squares feel too crowded.
markets.walk: Fifteen minutes on foot from Chamissoplatz along Bergmannstraße.

markets.name: Karl-Marx-Allee
markets.line: A modest market set against the Stalinist boulevard, which is the real reason to walk down here.
markets.walk: The only central market that runs on both midweek quiet days.

markets.name: Markthalle Neun
markets.line: An 1891 covered hall, so this is the one that works in rain and the only real option on a Monday.
markets.walk: Closed on Sundays like every other market in this list.

markets.name: Street Food Thursday
markets.line: The Thursday evening cook-up inside Markthalle Neun, and the latest market hours in the city.
markets.walk: Starts as the daytime traders pack down.

dayNotes.mon: Monday is the empty day. One covered hall is trading and nothing else on this list is.
dayNotes.tue: A quiet day that turns good after 11:00, when the two Neukölln and Kreuzberg markets open.
dayNotes.wed: The classic Berlin market morning. Both big squares shut early in the afternoon.
dayNotes.thu: The best spread of the week, and the only day that runs from noon to 22:00 without a gap.
dayNotes.fri: A late-start day. Nothing here opens before 11:00, so a slow morning costs you nothing.
dayNotes.sat: Peak market day. Nine markets, all of them shut by 18:00.
dayNotes.sun: No weekly food market in Berlin trades on a Sunday. Sunday belongs to the flea markets instead.
